title: Model Flavor Thermometer & Compatibility Lab
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a concise operational analysis and test harness that maps 'model flavors' (latency-optimized, cost-optimized, high-consistency, quant-friendly) against real Redwood production workloads and a synthetic enterprise workload suite. Produce a single-page Thermometer deliverable that shows where each model flavor sits along practical axes (median P50 latency, token cost per 1k, output consistency score, quantization degradation delta). Pair that with a Compatibility Lab matrix that records integration friction: SDK surface parity, function-calling behavior differences, streaming edge cases, and quantization/hardware compatibility notes.
objectives: Define a 4-axis operational taxonomy for model flavors relevant to Redwood customers
Run 10 representative synthetic workloads and 6 anonymized customer workload samples through a compatibility harness
Produce a Thermometer deliverable and a Compatibility Lab matrix with actionable procurement triggers
success_metrics: Thermometer published and reviewed by PM/Eng/DS within Cycle (one pager)
Compatibility matrix covers 12 model variants and 3 hardware classes (A100, H100, CPU tuned)
Three procurement triggers defined: fallback-safe, requires-quantization-validation, enterprise-ready
approach: Catalog candidate models and variants (open models + popular hosted variants)
Define synthetic workload templates: short chat, long-context summarization, retrieval-augmented Q&A, multi-turn dialog with tool calls
Execute workloads across hosted and dedicated infra, record latency/cost/consistency metrics
Run targeted compatibility checks for SDK call signatures, streaming chunking, and function-calling edge cases
Score and visualize results into Thermometer + Compatibility Lab deliverables
deliverables: Short memo with procurement triggers and recommended fallbacks
Demo runbook and scripts in GitHub (link in related_links)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: anonymized customer traces may be insufficiently diverse. Mitigation: augment with synthetic variations and request 2 more anonymized samples from Solutions team.
Risk: quantized model variants have inconsistent versioning. Mitigation: lock to specific artifact hashes and record provenance in the matrix.
Risk: results vary by infra. Mitigation: capture hardware tags and include normalization notes in deliverables.
